title: A wage-judgment debtor and a differently named City payee at one suite
question: Is a firm the City pays registered at the same suite as a differently named employer with a Labor Commissioner wage judgment?
finding: 462 judgments name a San Francisco address; 181 give a suite. At 3 suites a differently named business the City paid $100,000 or more after the judgment is registered beside the debtor. In 1 the two also use one trade name: Zenith Health Network LLC ($747,541 paid since) beside Mega Protect Services LLC (judgment J-93501 of 2025-01-27, $25,998, status open/unpaid; 2 more against people at the same suite on the same day). The rest are neighbours in multi-tenant suites.
how: the “planning records” analysis matched judgment debtors to City payees by name. Here the debtor's address is used instead: each judgment with a San Francisco suite is set against every business registered at that suite, and a differently named registrant is listed when the City paid it $100,000 or more in fiscal years from the judgment on. Suites with more than six registered accounts are skipped. A row is marked when the debtor and the payee are also registered under the same trade name.
limits: Sharing a suite is not sharing an owner; only the trade-name rows carry a second link, and even there the registry does not name officers. The judgment search warns that payments made directly to workers are often not recorded, so "open" may be paid. Judgments against people are counted and the person is not named.

columns.t: City paid it from the judgment year on

rows.tie: same suite, and both registered under the same trade name
